predecessors.name: Srivijaya
predecessors.text: Kedah, which Srivijaya held: 'the Buddhist Srivijaya kingdom was in direct control of Kedah'

predecessors.name: Kedah Kingdom
predecessors.text: the pre-Islamic Hindu-Buddhist kingdom of Kedah, whose ruler Phra Ong Mahawangsa converted to Islam

successors.name: British Colonial Empire
successors.text: Kedah, which 'became a British protectorate in 1909' by the Anglo-Siamese Treaty

ledger.x: 1136: Kedah becomes a sultanate when its ruler converts to Islam.

c. 1294: Kedah's outline grows to Satun and Songkhla (year is Cliopatria's; the page is silent). No other Cliopatria polity holds those cells in 1294-1458, hence 'nobody'; the Kedah Sultanate page says Kedah was under Srivijaya's direct control and, in the Thai chronicles, 'a Thai city like Nakhon Si Thammarat'…
1459: the northern strip passes to Ayutthaya in Cliopatria (page silent; the year is Cliopatria's).
1786: Francis Light takes possession of Penang for the East India Company.
1808: Siam creates the Kingdom of Setul Mambang Segara out of Kedah.
1842: the sultan is restored under Siamese suzerainty, without Perlis.
c. 1895: Cliopatria's shape gains one cell on its southern border from the British (it was Perak's in 1842-1876 and the British Colonial Empire's to 1894). No page opened mentions it.
1909: Setul is excluded from Kedah by the Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 9 July 1909 and stays with Siam (the Perlis page: 'Satun remained with Thailand').

wars.name: Aceh's attack on Kedah
wars.outcome: Sultan Sulaiman Shah was captured by Aceh in 1619; no territory is recorded as changing hands.

wars.name: Kedah-East India Company conflict over Penang
wars.outcome: The British held Penang; Kedah's 1791 army in Seberang Perai was beaten and a ceasefire signed in 1791; the 1800 treaty added Seberang Perai.

wars.name: Siamese conquest of Kedah and Kedahan resistance
wars.outcome: Siam annexed Kedah in November 1821 and ruled it through Ligor; Tengku Kudin retook Alor Setar briefly in 1831 and another resistance came in 1838; the sultan was restored in 1842 under Siamese suzerainty.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; the shapes are approximate cell outlines.
The border with Province Wellesley on the Perai River is sharp from 1800 ('turned the river into the international border'); the rest stays soft.
Kedah annexed by Siam; the sultan in exile in Penang; no Kedah territory of its own.
The partition lines with Perlis, Kubang Pasu and Setul are not described by any page opened.
